article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

tasks.prompt: What is the main idea of the article?
options: Eating normally discarded fruit and vegetable parts can add fibre and reduce food waste.
All fruit skins should be eaten raw without washing.
Adults should replace wholemeal bread with watermelon rind.
Cooking completely removes fibre from vegetables.
tasks.correct_answer: Eating normally discarded fruit and vegetable parts can add fibre and reduce food waste.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הרעיון המרכזי הוא ששימוש בחלקים שבדרך כלל נזרקים יכול להוסיף סיבים תזונתיים וגם לצמצם בזבוז מזון.

tasks.prompt: What percentage of adults meet the recommended 30g of fibre per day?
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לפי הנתונים הרשמיים, רק 4% מהמבוגרים מגיעים לכמות המומלצת של 30 גרם סיבים ביום.

tasks.prompt: Which discarded part contained five times more fibre than the part people usually eat?
options: Broccoli stalks
Watermelon rind
Butternut squash seeds
Pineapple skin and core
tasks.explanation_hebrew: במחקר נמצא שקליפת האננס והליבה הכילו פי חמישה יותר סיבים מבשר הפרי.

tasks.prompt: In the article, what does “root-to-tip” eating mean?
options: Eating only root vegetables
Using as much of a fruit or vegetable as possible
Removing every seed before cooking
Choosing food only from local farms
tasks.correct_answer: Using as much of a fruit or vegetable as possible
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בהקשר הכתבה, root-to-tip פירושו להשתמש בכמה שיותר חלקים של הפרי או הירק, כולל חלקים שבדרך כלל נזרקים.

tasks.prompt: Why does the dietitian suggest chopping, freezing and later using a broccoli stalk?
options: Because the stalk contains no fibre until it is frozen
Because useful food need not be discarded when it does not fit the current meal
Because frozen stalks become safe for young children
Because broccoli florets are unsuitable for soup
tasks.correct_answer: Because useful food need not be discarded when it does not fit the current meal
tasks.explanation_hebrew: העצה מראה שאפשר לשמור חלק מזין לשימוש עתידי במקום לזרוק אותו רק מפני שאינו מתאים לארוחה הנוכחית.

tasks.prompt: Which items does the British Nutrition Foundation say should be avoided entirely?
options: Kiwi skin and broccoli stalks
Pineapple cores and bell pepper seeds
Green potatoes and rhubarb leaves
Watermelon rind and squash seeds
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מזהירה שתפוחי אדמה ירוקים ועלי ריבס מכילים תרכובות רעילות ולכן יש להימנע מהם.

tasks.prompt: Give two examples from the study showing that discarded food parts can be rich in fibre.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שתי דוגמאות מדויקות, רצוי עם נתונים או השוואות מהכתבה.
expected_points: Watermelon rind contained 2.10g of fibre per 100g, about the amount in a slice of wholemeal bread.
Butternut squash skin and seeds contained 9.25g per 100g, nearly as much as a bowl of bran flakes.
Pineapple skin and core contained five times more fibre than the flesh.

tasks.prompt: Why does the article recommend increasing fibre gradually rather than changing the diet all at once?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את ההמלצה ולציין מי עלול להתקשות במיוחד.
expected_points: A sudden increase can cause bloating.
People with IBS may find extra fibre harder to tolerate.
A gradual change lets the body adjust while people test palatable options.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the benefits, practical suggestions and cautions of root-to-tip eating in 3–4 sentences.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך לכלול תועלת בריאותית, דרכי שימוש מעשיות ואזהרה אחת לפחות.
expected_points: Discarded skins, stalks, cores and seeds can provide substantial fibre and reduce waste.
Examples include leaving kiwi skin on, cooking broccoli stalks and blending pineapple cores.
Produce should be washed and some tough parts cooked or chopped.
Toxic parts such as green potatoes and rhubarb leaves should not be eaten.

tasks.prompt: Write a short practical message encouraging a hesitant friend to try one safe root-to-tip food idea.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לנסח מסר ברור ולא מוגזם, עם דוגמה בטוחה ועצה מעשית מהכתבה.
expected_points: Suggest one specific option such as kiwi skin, broccoli stalk in a stir-fry or pineapple core in a smoothie.
Mention a benefit such as extra fibre or less waste.
Include a safety step such as washing produce or increasing fibre gradually.
